title: Meta ads (creative concepts, copy, briefs, structure)

gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, review, customer, quote, UGC creator, press mention, scarcity or deadline that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Gaps are marked [NEEDS FACT: ...].

Limits and format: every hook complete within the first 125 characters of primary text; headlines ≤ 40 characters (flag any over 27); 3–5 concepts; each concept has primary text, 3 headlines, a CTA button and a creative brief.

Policy: no personal-attribute phrasing (race, religion, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, health, financial status, criminal record, name); no before-and-after body images or ideal-body implication; special ad category declared where the business fits one; no fake buttons or notifications.
Approval and budget: everything drafted as paused for owner approval; daily budget × 30.4 within the stated monthly budget; no promised results or guarantees the business hasn't confirmed.

anchors.1: Variants differ only in wording, colour or CTA; effectively one concept.
anchors.3: Two distinct angles; others are near-variants or share buyer and format.
anchors.5: 3–5 concepts, each differing from every other on at least two of buyer, angle and format, with visually distinct first frames.

anchors.1: Opens with brand name, throat-clearing or a personal-attribute question.
anchors.3: Clear but generic; could be any brand in the category.
anchors.5: Names a specific situation or outcome in VOC words, stands alone without 'See more', and the body pays it off.

anchors.1: No offer, or vague claims with no evidence.
anchors.3: Offer present; proof generic or far from the claim.
anchors.5: Offer, price or terms clear in headline and text; strongest confirmed proof in the first two lines.

anchors.1: No brief, or 'lifestyle image of product'.
anchors.3: Describes the visual but not the first 3 seconds, ratios or on-screen text.
anchors.5: Ratio(s), exact first 3 seconds, on-screen text for sound-off, shot list with real products and people, safe zones, end frame, and what the owner must film and how long it takes.

anchors.1: Banner-ad tone, hype words, emoji bullets, multiple exclamation marks.
anchors.5: Reads like a post from a real person; 'you' leads; short varied lines; no AI tells.

anchors.1: Angles picked with no link to buyers or VOC.
anchors.3: Angles plausible but evidence not stated.
anchors.5: Each concept names its buyer, awareness level and the VOC phrase, review theme or fact it rests on.

anchors.1: Small budget split across many ad sets or interests; no budget math.
anchors.3: Simple structure but optimisation event or learning-phase fit not considered.
anchors.5: One campaign and ad set for small budgets, budget math shown, optimisation event chosen against the ~50 events/week learning threshold, custom-audience exclusions set.

anchors.1: Advantage+ settings ignored; no test rule.
anchors.3: Settings mentioned; test rule vague ('see what works').
anchors.5: Each Advantage+ setting decided with a reason; pre-registered per-concept kill rule tied to the owner's target; refresh plan replaces losers with new concepts.
